title: Canada Fires Back: New Tariffs on U.S. Goods!
summary:
Have you ever had a fight with a friend where you both start doing mean things to each other? That's kind of what's happening between the U.S. and Canada right now. Canada is mad because the U.S. put big taxes on Canadian goods. So Canada is fighting back with its own taxes on U.S. products.

Starting September 8, Canada will add taxes (called tariffs) of 15% to 50% on over 700 U.S. products. That's like if a $10 toy suddenly cost $15. These products include steel, aluminum, home appliances, farm equipment, paper, and electronics. In total, it affects $27 billion worth of stuff.

The U.S. started this by putting 50% tariffs on about $20 billion of Canadian goods. President Trump even said he might put more tariffs on steel and cars next year. And he made a joke about changing the name of Lake Ontario to "Lake America." But Canada's industry minister said, "We will always call it Lake Ontario, period."

Even though they're fighting, President Trump admitted the U.S. really needs aluminum from Canada. He said, "We get it all from Canada for the most part, and we need it badly."

This trade war is already hurting some businesses. A furniture maker in Michigan named Michael Howard says he's losing customers. So this fight isn't just about big companies—it affects real people like him.

Why does this matter? The U.S. and Canada trade about $800 billion worth of goods every year. That's a lot! When they fight, it can make things more expensive and cause problems for workers and businesses on both sides. Hopefully, they can work it out soon!
why_it_matters: This trade fight can make prices go up for things like toys, electronics, and appliances, and it shows how decisions by leaders can affect families and jobs.

background_read: The United States and Canada are neighbors and two of each other's biggest trading partners.
Tariffs are extra fees countries charge on things they buy from other countries, and they can make products more expensive.
For many years, the U.S. and Canada have traded lots of goods like cars, steel, and food.
Article_Structure: WHO: Canada and the United States, including President Trump and Canada's industry minister.
WHAT: Canada is adding new tariffs on U.S. products after the U.S. put tariffs on Canadian goods.
WHERE: The fight is between the U.S. and Canada, and it affects goods crossing the border like steel, aluminum, and electronics.
WHY: Canada is fighting back to protect its own businesses, and the fight is already hurting real people like furniture maker Michael Howard.

perspectives.description: Canada is fighting back with tariffs to stand up for its own products and workers.
President Trump says the U.S. needs Canadian aluminum, but he still wants to pressure Canada about trade.
People like Michael Howard are losing customers and getting hurt by the trade fight.
